title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
description:
Given the `root` of a binary search tree (BST) and an integer `k`, return the `k`-th smallest value (**1-indexed**) among all the node values in the tree.

All node values in the BST are distinct.
constraints: The number of nodes in the tree is n.
All node values in the BST are unique.
hints: An inorder traversal (left, root, right) of a BST visits nodes in strictly ascending order.
Use an iterative stack-based inorder traversal so you can stop immediately upon visiting the k-th node instead of traversing the entire tree.
This achieves O(h + k) time and O(h) space, where h is the height of the tree.

examples.explanation: The sorted values in the BST are [1, 2, 3, 4], so the 1st smallest element is 1.
The sorted values are [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], so the 3rd smallest element is 3.
The sorted values are [2, 5, 7, 10, 12, 15, 20], so the 6th smallest element is 15.
